//: memory-search hook data — maps 'which memory to inject when a given file is edited'.
//engine: The engine (core) hardcodes nothing. This file is the per-project data. Delete it and the hook is a no-op.
//format: glob=fnmatch, contains=substring (case-insensitive), match_empty=also match edits with no path, command_contains=substring of the raw shell command, memory=path relative to .claude/memory/
//scope: Path keys (glob, contains, match_empty) are read only for file edits; command_contains only for shell commands. They never cross over — otherwise a contains rule would also fire on read-only commands such as grep.
//example: The rules below are a Kotlin/Spring example. Adapt them to your project. A memory file must actually exist to be injected (missing files are skipped silently).
